business_scope.primary_industry_name: Marine Heavy Driving of Wind Farm Monopile Foundations

Convention between the Kingdom of Spain and the People's Republic of China for the Avoidance of Double Taxation and the Prevention of Fiscal Evasion with respect to Taxes on Income and on Capital (in force from 24 May 1992)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Ley 10/2010, de 28 de abril, de prevención del blanqueo de capitales y de la financiación del terrorismo; Real Decreto 304/2014, de 5 de mayo, por el que se aprueba el Reglamento de la Ley 10/2010; Orden JUS/319/2018, de 21 de marzo, por la que se crea y regula el Registro de Titularidades Reales; transposing Directive (EU) 2015/849 as amended by Directive (EU) 2018/843 (AMLD4/AMLD5).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of the passport or national identity document, and foreign tax identification / NIE evidence of each director, shareholder and ultimate beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National passport/identity authority; Spanish consulate or Dirección General de Policía for NIE
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille on certified copies; sworn translation into Spanish

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of incorporation and good standing / company register excerpt of any corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent foreign Companies Registry or equivalent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille, or consular legalization where the country of origin is not party to the Apostille Convention; sworn translation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarial power of attorney for the person appointed to execute the incorporation deed before the Spanish notary
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary in the country of origin or a Spanish notary
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization; if granted in Spain, notarized directly in Spanish

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter or source-of-funds statement covering the corporate capital contribution
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Account-holding bank or licensed financial institution
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Certified by the issuing bank; notarized or apostilled where required by the notary; sworn translation

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of directors, shareholders, UBOs and counterparties against the SEPBLAC/National Anti-Money-Laundering databases, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, UN Consolidated List, and OFAC SDN List. Politically exposed persons, their family members and close associates require enhanced due diligence and senior-management approval under articles 14 and 15 of Ley 10/2010, with continuous transaction monitoring and documentation retention for at least 10 years.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Sede Electrónica del Colegio de Registradores de España – Registro Mercantil Central, Denominación Social section (www.registradores.org / rmc.registradores.org)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The proposed company name must be written in Spanish using the Spanish alphabet. Non-Spanish expressions must be transliterated into Spanish spelling and are admissible only if they are in ordinary commercial use, are not misleading, do not infringe third-party rights, and do not contravene Spanish law, public order, or the official character of state institutions.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection of a proposed name, the applicant may file a reconsideration request (recurso de reposición) before the same registral authority within one month, and thereafter a hierarchical appeal before the Dirección General de Seguridad Jurídica y Fe Pública. Alternatively, a fresh application for a negative name certificate may be submitted with a new proposed name. If all administrative remedies are exhausted, the applicant may bring a judicial action before the Juzgado de lo Mercantil of the relevant province. The negative name certificate must be used to execute the notarial deed within its 90-day validity; no formal extension is available, and a new certificate must be obtained if it expires.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is not acceptable as the sole statutory registered office of an SL. The registered office and tax domicile must be a physical premises situated in Spain where actual management, representation, or administrative operations are located. For offshore wind turbine piling activities, a service-based virtual address may be used only as a supplementary correspondence channel, not as the registered office.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Moderate. Estimated 35% annual probability of an unannounced inspection of the registered office by the Tax Agency or registry authorities if the address lacks genuine operational substance. Offshore piling work sites face a higher likelihood, approximately 60%, of unannounced inspections by labour, maritime, and environmental authorities due to the high-risk nature of marine heavy construction.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory notarial tariff calculated on deed pages and stated capital; typical low-capital SL range USD 450–USD 900

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Registro de Titularidades Reales / Colegio de Registradores
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory registry filing and notarial handling tariff

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille or consular legalization of foreign corporate and identity documents, and sworn Spanish translation

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Per-document consular fee and sworn translation market rate

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: AML/CFT KYC screening, PEP and sanctions list checks (OFAC, UN, EU, SEPBLAC) for directors, shareholders and UBOs

Registered office address and commercial correspondence support service – first 12 months

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarized and sworn translation of foreign documents into Spanish, including company objects and shareholder resolutions
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official sworn translation tariff and notary attestation market benchmark

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Royal Legislative Decree 1/2010 approving the consolidated text of the Spanish Companies Act (Ley de Sociedades de Capital), principally Articles 4, 20-24, 28-32, 58-63, 210-242, and 253-284; Royal Decree 1784/1996, approving the Mercantile Registry Regulations; Law 14/2013 on entrepreneurs and the CIRCE electronic incorporation system.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: The competent Mercantile Registry (Registro Mercantil) for the company's provincial registered office, coordinated where applicable through the Central Mercantile Registry (Registro Mercantil Central) and the CIRCE system administered by the Directorate-General for Industry and Small and Medium Enterprises.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Public deed of incorporation (escritura pública de constitución) filed with the competent provincial Mercantile Registry, supported by the certified name-clearance certificate and tax identification documentation.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: The statutory minimum capital of a Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada is EUR 1.00. Contributions must be fully assumed and paid at incorporation. Until the company reaches EUR 3,000 in capital, at least 20% of annual profit must be allocated to legal reserve and, on liquidation with insufficient assets, shareholders may have additional liability up to the difference between EUR 3,000 and the subscribed capital. No statutory escrow account is required for an SL; a bank certificate evidencing monetary contributions may be used, although founders may dispense with that certificate and remain jointly liable for the reality of the contributions. Notarial, registry, name-reservation, publication, tax, and professional fees are separate from any official filing-fee estimate.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: The Board resolves that: (1) the Company accepts and confirms the subscriptions and fully paid contributions for the quotas stated in the deed of incorporation and articles; (2) the registered office is adopted at the address recorded in the deed, with authority delegated to the sole director or managing directors to file changes; (3) [Name] is appointed sole director/managing director, as applicable, accepting office and declaring no legal impediment; (4) [Name] is appointed secretary, if applicable; and (5) the officers are authorized to obtain the NIF, complete Mercantile Registry filings, open bank accounts, and execute all documents necessary for commencement of business.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Reserve the Corporate Name and Confirm Beneficial Ownership
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Central Mercantile Registry (Registro Mercantil Central), including its online name-certification service
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit up to five proposed names, obtain the negative name certificate, and ensure that the certificate remains valid for execution and filing of the incorporation deed. Prepare the ultimate beneficial owner chain, foreign shareholder identification, and powers of attorney. Apostille or legalize foreign public documents and provide sworn Spanish translations where required.
required_dossiers: Foreign shareholder corporate certificates and constitutional documents
Passports or national identity documents of shareholders, directors, and beneficial owners
Apostilled or legalized powers of attorney
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected or the filing is queried, submit an alternative reserved name, correct identity or beneficial ownership data, and refile within the certificate validity period. Replace defective foreign documents with legalized and translated versions.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execute the Public Deed of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Spanish notary public (notario) selected by the incorporators, with electronic coordination through CIRCE where used
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Provide the notary with the name certificate, articles of association, shareholder and director identification, NIF or NIE details, registered-office evidence, and contribution evidence or the statutory waiver of bank certification. Execute the public deed in Spanish or through an authorized sworn translation. Ensure that the corporate purpose expressly covers marine construction, offshore installation, piling, engineering, equipment handling, and related ancillary activities.
required_dossiers: Shareholder identification and powers of attorney
Registered-office title, lease, or occupancy evidence
Bank contribution certificate or statutory waiver
Foreign corporate approvals and legalized documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Cure notarial observations by amending the deed, articles, powers, translations, or contribution evidence. If a shareholder cannot attend, issue a notarized and legalized power of attorney acceptable to the Spanish notary.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Tax Identification and Register the Company
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Spanish Tax Agency (Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria) and the provincial Mercantile Registry (Registro Mercantil Provincial)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Request the provisional NIF using Form 036 or the CIRCE process, submit the public deed electronically or through the notary, and file the incorporation with the provincial Mercantile Registry. After registration, obtain the definitive NIF and update the Tax Agency filing. Register the ultimate beneficial ownership information through the applicable notarial and Mercantile Registry channels.
required_dossiers: Proof of payment of registry and professional charges
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to a Mercantile Registry defect notice within the prescribed cure period, normally by rectifying the deed or filing a supplementary public deed. Re-submit corrected tax forms and obtain the definitive NIF after registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Complete Governance, Accounting, and Employment Registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Registry, Spanish Tax Agency, General Treasury of Social Security (Tesorería General de la Seguridad Social), and the relevant autonomous-community employment authority
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Legalize accounting books electronically through the Commercial Registry, file the beneficial ownership statement where required, register the company as an employer before hiring, obtain a Social Security contribution account code, and register employees and workplace risk-prevention arrangements. Adopt board and shareholder resolutions approving bank mandates, accounting policies, delegated authorities, and compliance controls.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct rejected electronic books or Social Security filings, provide missing signatures or identity data, and resubmit through the relevant authority portal. Do not commence employment before employer registration and employee enrollment are complete.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register Industrial Activity and Secure Project-Specific Marine Authorizations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry for Industry and Tourism, Directorate-General for Industry; Ministry for the Ecological Transition and the Demographic Challenge; Directorate-General for the Coast and the Sea; relevant Port Authority; and the competent autonomous-community and local authorities
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Determine whether the company's premises or equipment constitute an industrial establishment requiring registration in the Integrated Industrial Registry (Registro Integrado Industrial) or an autonomous-community industrial notification. For each offshore project, obtain the applicable maritime-space, coastal-domain, port, navigation, construction, electrical, environmental, occupation, and safety authorizations before mobilization. A separate national manufacturing permit is not automatically required merely to incorporate an SL; licensing depends on the physical facility and project scope.
required_dossiers: Technical project signed by competent engineers
Site, port, seabed, and cable-route information
Marine traffic and navigation risk assessment
Corporate deed, NIF, and beneficial ownership documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Answer technical and environmental information requests within the stated period, amend the project, conduct public-participation responses, and appeal an express refusal through the applicable administrative review or contentious-administrative procedure. No work should begin while a mandatory authorization remains pending.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry for Industry and Tourism, Directorate-General for Industry, together with the competent autonomous-community industrial authority; offshore project authorizations additionally involve the Ministry for the Ecological Transition and the Demographic Challenge, the Directorate-General for the Coast and the Sea, the relevant Port Authority, and competent local authorities.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No single universal national operating license applies to all offshore monopile-installation contractors. Depending on the activity, required instruments may include industrial-establishment registration or responsible declaration, municipal opening or activity authorization, port occupation authorization, coastal public-domain concession, maritime-space compatibility authorization, construction authorization, and project-specific administrative authorization for the wind-farm electrical installation under Law 24/2013 and Royal Decree 1955/2000.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry for the Ecological Transition and the Demographic Challenge, Directorate-General for Environmental Quality and Assessment, with the competent autonomous-community environmental body where jurisdiction is transferred
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Normally Full Ordinary Environmental Impact Assessment for offshore wind-farm projects and associated marine infrastructure falling within Annex I or otherwise designated for ordinary assessment under Law 21/2013 on Environmental Assessment. Separate screening or assessment may apply to a contractor's yard, port works, dredging, cable routes, Natura 2000 sites, and marine public-domain occupation.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Comply with the authorization-specific limits under the Water Law and Royal Decree 849/1986 for wastewater discharges; obtain discharge permits before releasing process or contaminated water. Manage hazardous and non-hazardous waste under Law 7/2022 and Royal Decree 553/2020, using authorized waste operators and traceability records. Control VOCs, dust, noise, underwater piling noise, fuel, oil, and spill risks under the applicable environmental permit, port rules, and project conditions; no generic nationwide VOC threshold replaces the permit-specific limits. Apply Best Available Techniques where an integrated environmental authorization is required.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Before operation, obtain or document the applicable municipal fire-prevention and opening authorization, emergency and self-protection plan under Royal Decree 393/2007 where applicable, and certification of fire-protection systems under Royal Decree 513/2017. Obtain structural, lifting, electrical, pressure-equipment, machinery, and temporary-works inspections required by the technical project and applicable industrial-safety regulations. Comply with Law 31/1995 on Occupational Risk Prevention, Royal Decree 1627/1997 for construction works, maritime work and diving rules where applicable, worker training, medical surveillance, personal protective equipment, contractor coordination, and port emergency requirements.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT), official portal https://www.agenciatributaria.gob.es/
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Foreign entities register with the AEAT to obtain a NIF. Submit Form 036 (for non-residents) or equivalent through a tax representative or online if eligible, including corporate documents, proof of legal existence, and Spanish business activity. Processing typically takes 15-30 days.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box elections; Spain operates a territorial tax system with entity-level taxation for resident companies. Hybrid mismatch provisions under EU ATAD apply for certain structures.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory electronic invoicing (facturación electrónica) with real-time data transmission to AEAT. Digital stamps and clearance via the integrated platform; non-compliant invoices rejected. API integration required for large taxpayers.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: 0% VAT applies to goods exported outside the EU and services supplied to non-EU customers. Requires proof that goods/services leave the EU territory and are not consumed in Spain.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Bill of Lading or equivalent transport document
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Claims of fraudulent zero-rating lead to VAT reassessment, interest, fines (up to 100% of tax evaded), and potential criminal liability. Retrospective clawback with surcharges for non-compliance.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de España (Bank of Spain); foreign-exchange policy and payment-system rules are also governed by applicable European Union law and, where relevant, the European Central Bank and the Spanish Ministry of Economy, Trade and Business.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Spain uses the euro and applies the EU framework for free movement of capital and payments. There are no general foreign-exchange controls on current-account payments, capital contributions, dividends, or repatriation of investment proceeds. Banks must conduct sanctions, anti-money-laundering, source-of-funds, and payment-purpose checks. Dividend remittances remain subject to distributable-profit, corporate-approval, withholding-tax, and treaty or EU relief requirements. Foreign investment and cross-border transaction reporting may apply; reporting is not, by itself, an exchange-control approval or a restriction on remittance.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Spain has no general statutory export-proceeds surrender requirement, mandatory conversion ratio, or deadline requiring exporters to convert foreign-currency receipts into euros. Receipts may be retained in permitted foreign-currency accounts. Applicable bank reporting, Banco de España statistical reporting, tax, customs, sanctions, and documentation obligations still apply. Confirm transaction-specific reporting thresholds and filing duties with the bank and Spanish advisers.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account; project-specific escrow or controlled account subject to bank approval
Operational Account; project-specific escrow or controlled account subject to bank approval
Operational Account; project-specific escrow or controlled account subject to bank approval

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium for routine euro payments and eligible foreign-currency services, subject to the provider's geographic coverage, account terms, and risk appetite. An EU-authorized electronic money institution is not a bank, and safeguarded e-money is not equivalent to a bank deposit or necessarily covered by a deposit-guarantee scheme. Do not rely on an EMI as the sole project-finance, escrow, or letter-of-credit provider. Verify authorization, safeguarding arrangements, payment limits, and correspondent-bank access.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: No universal Spanish statutory rule requires every director to appear physically to open a corporate account. Banks set their own onboarding standards and may require an in-person meeting, wet-ink documents, or enhanced verification, particularly for non-resident owners, complex ownership, or high-value project flows. Remote onboarding may be available after identity verification and acceptance of certified or apostilled corporate documents. Obtain bank confirmation before relying on remote opening.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident, layered, nominee, or trust ownership; inability to identify the ultimate beneficial owner.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Current Spanish company registry extract and constitutional documents; complete ownership chart through all intermediate entities to natural-person beneficial owners; UBO register evidence; identity and address documents; corporate registries and good-standing evidence for foreign owners; certified translations, apostilles, or legalizations as requested; board resolutions and authorized-signatory evidence.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large initial capital payment or project funding inconsistent with the company profile or originating from an unrelated third party.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed subscription, shareholder-loan, or financing documents; board approvals; bank statements and audited accounts evidencing source of funds; originator and beneficiary account details; payment instructions identifying the legal purpose; group structure and related-party explanation; supporting tax and investment-reporting records where applicable.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear offshore-wind project purpose, unusually large trade payments, or counterparties in higher-risk jurisdictions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Project contracts, tender or concession documents, permits and license status, purchase orders, invoices, bills of lading or delivery records, counterparty due-diligence results, beneficial-ownership and sanctions screening, payment schedule, and a reconciliation of each payment to the project budget.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Payments involving sanctioned parties, restricted goods, high-risk intermediaries, or inconsistent payment narratives.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Documented sanctions and export-control screening; end-user and end-use statements where relevant; contractual representations; logistics and vessel documentation; approved bank payment purpose and supporting invoice; escalation records and evidence that no restricted person or activity is involved.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Expected turnover, currencies, jurisdictions, or payment volumes differ materially from the onboarding profile.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Updated business plan, annual project cash-flow forecast, expected transaction volumes and corridors, customer and supplier schedules, source-of-funds and source-of-wealth evidence, tax registrations, and prompt written updates to the bank.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Route shareholder equity and documented shareholder loans from an account held in the investor's own name to the Spanish SL's corporate account through SEPA Credit Transfer for euro payments or SWIFT for non-SEPA or foreign-currency payments. Use accurate remitter and beneficiary names, the Spanish company's legal name and IBAN, and a truthful payment reference identifying share capital, share premium, or loan funding. Provide subscription or loan agreements, corporate approvals, source-of-funds evidence, and bank-requested purpose documentation before transfer. Record the transaction in the company's books and complete applicable Spanish foreign-investment or statistical declarations; do not treat a bank payment-purpose label as a substitute for a legally required filing.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Use SEPA Credit Transfer for eligible euro payments within SEPA and SWIFT cross-border payment instructions for other currencies or destinations; banks may process SWIFT messages under ISO 20022 rather than legacy MT103 formatting. Match each payment to the executed contract, invoice, purchase order, shipping or milestone evidence, and the agreed beneficiary account. For material equipment or construction procurement, request an irrevocable documentary commercial letter of credit subject to agreed UCP 600 terms, with presentation requirements, expiry, shipment or milestone conditions, and discrepancy procedures settled before issuance. Consider documentary collections or bank guarantees where commercially suitable. Reconcile fees, exchange rates, value dates, and beneficiary receipts.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable foreign-exchange forwards with an authorized bank or eligible investment firm, supported by documented underlying exposure and subject to suitability, collateral, and reporting requirements.
Foreign-exchange swaps for documented short-term liquidity or currency-management needs, subject to counterparty limits and applicable EMIR, MiFID II, and bank documentation requirements.

Non-deliverable forwards only where legally and commercially available for the relevant currency pair; settlement and counterparty terms must be reviewed because NDFs are not a substitute for a prohibited or unavailable currency conversion.

Currency options or cross-currency swaps may be considered for documented project exposures, subject to product eligibility, valuation, collateral, accounting, and applicable derivatives reporting obligations.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders’ meeting of the Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the financial year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to approve and file accounts may result in directors’ liability, registry closure after the filing deadline, and administrative fines generally ranging from EUR 1,200 to EUR 60,000, subject to statutory adjustments.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Deposit of annual financial statements and management report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after shareholder approval; for a calendar year-end, normally by 30 July
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Registry closure may prevent registration of most subsequent corporate documents. Fines may range from EUR 1,200 to EUR 60,000, with higher limits for larger companies. Spain has no routine automatic strike-off solely for late accounts, but prolonged inactivity or non-compliance may support dissolution or other registry and tax measures.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within the first 25 calendar days following the six-month period after the tax year-end; normally 1–25 July for a calendar year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalties depend on whether the return is filed voluntarily or after notice, and whether tax is payable. Late payment generally triggers surcharges, interest, and potentially tax penalties.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within four months after the financial year-end; normally by 30 April for a calendar year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or omitted legalization may impair evidentiary value of accounting records and may contribute to directors’ liability and enforcement exposure. The registry may reject or delay subsequent filings where statutory books are deficient.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Competent Registro Mercantil through the annual accounts filing process
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Submitted with the annual accounts and updated whenever beneficial ownership information changes
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Inaccurate, incomplete, or outdated beneficial ownership data may result in filing rejection, registry closure, administrative enforcement, and anti-money-laundering compliance exposure.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual statistical and related tax-information returns, where applicable
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Deadlines vary by form and facts, commonly during January, February, or the first quarter following the reporting year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file or inaccurate filing may trigger fixed or percentage-based penalties, late-filing surcharges, interest, and information-request procedures.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: An independent statutory audit is generally mandatory when the company exceeds at least two of the following thresholds for two consecutive financial years: total assets of EUR 2.85 million, annual net turnover of EUR 5.7 million, or average workforce of more than 50 employees. Audit obligations may also arise from regulated status, securities-market requirements, consolidation, public funding, or specific sector legislation.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Spanish General Accounting Plan (Spanish GAAP). IFRS-EU is mandatory for consolidated accounts of listed groups and may apply to other consolidated groups under Spanish law; it is not the default framework for an ordinary Spanish SL’s individual accounts.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The company must maintain accurate beneficial ownership information, report the beneficial owner through the annual accounts filing, and update the information when ownership or control changes. Share transfers must be recorded in the Register of Members and reflected in the beneficial ownership information where the change affects ultimate control. Notarial and anti-money-laundering identification requirements may apply to relevant transactions.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Directors and powers of representation
Register of contracts with the sole shareholder, if applicable
Accounting books and supporting accounting records

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: Approximately USD 350–1,500 per year, depending on registered-office, mail-handling, corporate-secretarial, and local representative services
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Approximately USD 4,000–20,000 per year for a non-listed operating SL; complex offshore construction, project-finance, consolidation, or multinational reporting may require a higher fee

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% general corporate income tax rate (Impuesto sobre Sociedades) applicable to Sociedades de Responsabilidad Limitada.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: 15% reduced rate for newly created companies during the first two tax periods with a positive taxable base if they conduct an economic activity; tax credits for R&D and innovation (up to 25% base credit plus supplementary 17% when exceeding prior-year thresholds), creation of employment, and reinvestment of extraordinary profits; corporate exemptions/integration relief for qualifying dividends and intra-group gains under Art. 21 and 56 LIS.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Unlimited (no statutory expiration period; annual offset limitations apply based on net turnover, generally capped at 60% of the positive taxable base for entities under EUR 20 million turnover and 25% for entities above the threshold, subject to an absolute minimum of EUR 1 million).

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Modelo 200 (Impuesto sobre Sociedades) – mandatory electronic filing via the AEAT Sede Electrónica (Spanish Tax Agency online portal), using secure authentication certificate or user credential.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual definitive return (Modelo 200); quarterly advance payments (pagos fraccionados) are due via Modelo 202 in April, October and December, each covering a portion of the annual corporate income tax liability.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a fiscal year closed on 31 December, the annual Modelo 200 return must be filed and paid by 25 July of the following year. For a non-calendar fiscal year, the filing deadline is the 25th day after the lapse of six months from the fiscal year-end.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxpayer identification (NIF), full legal name, registered address, and fiscal residence declarations; also the Spanish branch data where applicable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a Spanish SL with non-resident shareholders, enter the SL as the taxable entity. Non-resident shareholders without a permanent establishment in Spain do not file Modelo 200; they are subject to Spanish Non-Resident Income Tax (IRNR) on Spanish-source income through specific IRNR forms.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Primary CNAE activity code and, where applicable, separate line items for construction, installation services, and other income attributable to a permanent establishment or to foreign operations.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The Spanish SL must record the CNAE code corresponding to marine construction/offshore wind turbine pilings, e.g. CNAE 4291 / 4390. Non-resident shareholders should not be shown as taxpayers unless they have a Spanish permanent establishment through which the wind piling activity is economically carried out.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Start from the accounting net profit/loss, then apply all extra-accounting adjustments (permanent and temporary differences, depreciation/amortisation, provisions, impairment losses, and tax-exempt income).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Prepared from the Spanish statutory financial statements of the SL. Transactions with non-resident related parties must be adjusted for transfer pricing differences using arm’s length values; the corresponding adjustments are shown in the reconciliation to taxable base.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 4 – Taxable base and tax losses
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Resulting taxable income after integrating current-year adjustments and offsetting prior-year negative tax bases, showing any utilisation of available tax loss carryforwards.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only the SpanishSL’s taxable base is declared. Non-resident shareholders cannot offset losses of the Spanish SL against their own foreign-source income, and any dividend distribution to non-residents is subject to withholding at the time the profits are deemed distributed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 5 – Total tax, credits, and payments
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final gross tax due, application of tax credits (including double-taxation relief and R&D credits), withheld taxes, quarterly instalments, and the resulting amount to pay or to request for refund.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign tax credits for tax paid by the SL in other jurisdictions are computed in this SL. Withholding taxes on outbound dividends, interest, or royalties paid to non-residents are not calculated on Modelo 200 but are declared by the paying entity through the quarterly withholding declarations (Modelo 216/123) and annual returns.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late or non-filed Modelo 200 triggers late-filing surcharges under Art. 27 LGT (5% within 3 months; 10% within 6 months; 15% within 12 months; 20% after 12 months) plus late-payment interest. If the tax authority formally demands filing, the penalties escalate to 50% of the full amount due under Art. 191 LGT, or 100-150% if fraudulent, obstructionist, or for serious infractions; in addition, missing or inaccurate data may attract fixed-per-item fines.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 24% for dividends paid to non-residents without a Spanish permanent establishment under the general Non-Resident Income Tax rate; 19% for residents of an EU/EEA state with effective exchange of tax information; reduced to 0% under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive for qualifying corporate shareholders holding at least 5% of the Spanish SL, and potentially 0-15% under a bilateral tax treaty (DTA).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The non-resident shareholder must provide a valid Certificate of Tax Residence (TRC) from its jurisdiction of tax residence to the Spanish SL before the dividend payment; the Spanish SL then applies the relevant DTA rate as the withholding agent at source, retaining documentation for at least 4 years. If tax is withheld at a higher statutory rate, the non-resident must claim the excess refund via Modelo 210 (IRNR) before the AEAT, submitting the TRC, a certificate of beneficial ownership, and evidence of treaty eligibility; the period to request refunds is generally 4 years from the due date of the return, and the claim is subject to anti-abuse/principal-purpose tests under the Multilateral Instrument (MLI).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory WHT on royalties paid to non-residents: 24% (general) / 19% (EU/EEA); statutory WHT on interest paid to non-residents: 24% (general) / 19% (EU/EEA) unless interest is classified as bank-account interest in Spain where special rules may apply. Treaty and EU rates may reduce royalties and interest to 0% under the EU Interest and Royalties Directive for associated EU companies, or to 5-10% under many Spanish DTAs (including the Spain-Chile DTA as relevant for Latin American connections); all relief requires proof of beneficial ownership and a valid TRC.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 250,000 (aggregate related-party transactions threshold for the Spanish Local File); Master File is required when the ultimate parent’s consolidated group revenue exceeds EUR 45,000,000; Country-by-Country Report is required for groups with consolidated revenue equal to or above EUR 750,000,000.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: No standalone Economic Substance Regulations statute exists in Spain; however, economic substance is an operational requirement through the general anti-abuse clause (Art. 15 LGT), simulation/nullity rules, CFC rules, anti-hybrid rules, and the Principal Purpose Test under the MLI. A Spanish SL engaged in offshore wind turbine piling must demonstrate actual operational substance (office/premises, qualified employees, project management, engineering/installation decision-making, financing and risk assumption). If the SL is a conduit with no real activity, the tax authority may deny treaty benefits and recharacterize the flow as a sham distribution subject to penalties and possible criminal charges.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion (Delito contra la Hacienda Pública)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Intentionally concealing revenue from offshore wind piling operations, falsifying project costs, shifting profits through aggressive intercompany invoicing, or using round-tripping transactions to lower or eliminate the Spanish corporate income tax liability.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal: imprisonment from 1 to 5 years plus a proportional fine of 2 to 6 times the defrauded tax amount where the defrauded amount exceeds EUR 120,000; aggravated if the amount exceeds EUR 600,000 or international tax fraud is proven, with imprisonment increased to 2 to 6 years and fines of 6 to 12 times the defrauded amount. Administrative: proportional penalty of 50%-100% of the missing amount, increased to 100%-150% in cases of obstruction or material dissimulation of facts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors can be held jointly and severally liable for the tax debts and penalty surcharges if they caused or induced the valuation/manipulation; in criminal proceedings, the court may impose personal imprisonment, travel bans, asset embargoes, and disqualification from managing public or corporate funds.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Artificial Arrangement / Sham Structure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the Spanish SL as a letterbox entity with no employees, no operational premises, no independent management, and no real risk-taking solely to channel offshore wind installation proceeds into an ultimate non-resident parent while claiming treaty benefits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Spanish tax authorities may disregard the arrangement under the general anti-abuse rule (Art. 15 LGT), apply the arm’s length principle to re-attribute income, deny treaty relief under the MLI Principal Purpose Test, and assess back taxes plus late-payment interest and penalties of 50%-100% of the adjusted amount; the entity may additionally be re-qualified as having a permanent establishment in Spain for the non-resident parent.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and formal shareholders may be held personally liable for the re-assessed tax and penalties if they knowingly participated in the artificial scheme; in severe cases, the criminal tax evasion threshold can be reached, leading to imprisonment, travel restrictions, and disqualification orders.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting or transmitting project financing wire transfers and Letter of Credit payments on behalf of undisclosed third parties, failing to conduct know-your-customer and beneficial-owner checks, or deliberately structuring cash flows in EUR amounts below reporting thresholds to conceal the origin of funds from construction project payments.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fines for serious and very serious AML offences under Spanish Law 10/2010 range from EUR 60,001 to EUR 5,000,000 depending on the type and persistence of the violation (very serious infractions can reach the greater of EUR 150,001 or 2% of the offending institution’s resources). Criminal money laundering (Art. 301 Penal Code) can impose imprisonment from 6 months to 6 years and fines; assets and profits connected to the offence are confiscated.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, beneficial owners, and compliance officers can face personal criminal prosecution, imprisonment, and individual fines; courts may order preventive embargoes of personal and corporate assets and travel bans during the investigation; directors who fail to maintain an adequate AML prevention system in the SL are personally exposed to administrative fines and civil damages.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Documentation Failure and Arm’s-Length Misstatement
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to prepare, file, or retain Local File/Master File for intercompany transactions such as charter hire of piling vessels, project management fees, royalties for offshore foundation technology, or group services; alternatively, knowingly charging a non-arm’s length price and failing to contemporaneously document the basis.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Failure to provide required TP documentation triggers administrative penalties per Art. 186 LGT: between EUR 1,000 and EUR 15,000 per incident/document depending on the type and completeness of the documentation, and the AEAT can re-assess the taxable base at arm’s length with late-payment interest and a 50%-100% proportional penalty on the additional tax; if the correction results in a tax shortfall exceeding EUR 120,000 and is intentional, criminal tax evasion risk materialises.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign false or incomplete TP documentation, knowingly approve unfair intercompany prices, or fail to implement the required transfer pricing controls can be held personal civil partners of the corporate penalty; in criminal cases, the director can be imprisoned and disqualified from acting as a legal representative or administer third-party assets.
